title: Entity states
summary: Added, Unchanged, Modified, Deleted and Detached: how the context decides what SaveChanges does.

steps.title: The change tracker
body: Every entity the context knows has a **state**:
| `Added` | new, not in the database yet | `INSERT` |
| `Modified` | loaded, then a property changed | `UPDATE` of the changed columns |
| `Detached` | the context does not know it | nothing |

When a query returns an entity, the context stores it as `Unchanged` along with a **snapshot** of its original values. At `SaveChanges` it compares each tracked entity with its snapshot (*DetectChanges*) to find what is `Modified`, and after saving, everything becomes `Unchanged` again (deleted ones become `Detached`).

code: var pen = new Item { Name = "pen", Stock = 10 };
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db");
steps.explain: A new object is unknown (`Detached`) until `Add`. Saving turns `Added` into `Unchanged`. Changing a property makes it `Modified` (`Entry` runs change detection when you ask). `Remove` marks it `Deleted`, and after the `DELETE` the context forgets it.

steps.prompt: You load 10,000 rows with a tracking query just to show them on a page, then call `SaveChanges` at the end of the request out of habit. What does tracking cost you?
options: Memory for 10,000 entities plus their snapshots, and a DetectChanges pass over all of them in SaveChanges
Nothing: tracking is free until you change something
A table lock for the duration of the request
steps.explain: Tracking keeps a snapshot of every entity and compares them all on `SaveChanges`. For read-only data, use `AsNoTracking()` or a projection, as in module 4.

steps.title: Restock report
prompt: The tests give you `ShopDb` with `Items` (`Id`, `Name`, `Stock`, `PriceCents`). Write

that loads every item with `Stock` under 5, adds `amount` to its stock, and **before saving** returns a description of what will happen, one line per item ordered by name: `"ink: Stock 0 -> 5"` (use the tracker's original and current values). Then save, so the changes reach the database.
Items not under 5 must stay `Unchanged`: do not touch them.
solution: foreach (var item in low) item.Stock += amount;
